thread:
Alex W: follow-up on the soft-tiering sketch — thinking about avoiding physical slab moves by introducing a lightweight hot-bit + per-slab compactness score. intention: reduce cross-node handoffs but still favor hot prefixes in eviction.

Tess: sounds promising. how exactly do you envision the hot-bit interacting with existing eviction queues? bump priority, or special fast-path for re-reads?

Alex W: bump eviction score only. keep same queue structure but when allocator computes eviction weight it adds hot_bonus if hot-bit set. also maintain small per-slab hot FIFO to prefer recent promotions when doing localized compaction.

Miguel: two concerns: 1) correctness with concurrent writes during demote, 2) multi-tenant fairness. if hot-bit flips while a writer is mid-flight we could surface inconsistent KV.

Alex W: on correctness: prefix header carries a 32-bit gen; writers increment gen on commit. promotion/demotion will perform a gen publish fence (atomic store). readers that consult cache must check header.gen matches expected; on mismatch they fall back to authoritative read. we avoid checking gen on every hit by only validating when we cross an index boundary (i.e., when hot-bit changed) or when tombstone flags are present.

Samir: that conditional check helps, but it still adds checks in the demote path. What's the penalty under churn?

Alex W: microbench shows demote checks add ~200ns on the first post-demote miss, subsequent misses take normal RPC cost. demotes are rare for long-lived hot prefixes.

Tess: what about promotion signals? counters are expensive in header. can we use the sampler that telemetry already runs?

Miguel: yes — reuse access sampler. sampled hits accrue to a lightweight per-prefix bloom-like counter in memory (not persisted). use exponential decay window and threshold for promotion.

Samir: need tenant-level throttles. If a single tenant gets many promotions they might starve others.

Alex W: plan: per-tenant promotion tokens. each promotion consumes tokens; tokens replenish over time proportionally to tenant weight/SLA. tokens live in node-local tenant table to avoid global coordination.

Miguel: how do we handle handoff-era races? e.g., tenant moves between nodes and hot credits are stale.

Alex W: credits are local and conservative; when tenant migrates we reset local credits and fall back to default budget to avoid unfair carryover. migration is rare, and strictness avoids abuse.

Tess: telemetry/alerts? ops needs metrics to watch for oscillation.

Alex W: propose these metrics: hot_promotions_total, hot_demotion_total, hot_residency_seconds, gen_mismatch_counter, tenant_hot_credit_usage, hot_steal_rate. Add traces for promotion/demotion flows.

InfraBot: rollout guidance: implement behind feature flag; canary with small fraction of nodes for 2 weeks; add circuit breaker to disable soft-tiering if gen_mismatch_rate > 0.05 or hot_steal_rate > 0.1.

Samir: testing: stress with synthetic tenants that rapidly toggle hotness to detect oscillation and ensure backoff works. Also run multi-tenant fairness bench.

Miguel: runtime memory cost: adding hot-bit + 2-byte local counter + slab FIFO pointer ~adds 4-6 bytes/prefix. we should recalc based on 48B header variant.

Alex W: noted — I'll produce a mem-layout table. also adding an escape-hatch: if gen_mismatch spikes we flip to strict ownership transfers for affected slabs.

Tess: ok. please include APIs in RFC: prefix.header.gen, prefix.header.hotbit, PromotePrefix(idempotent RPC), and TenantHotCreditLease(resource_id).

Alex W: will draft RFC and prototype layout by Tue EOD. syncing Wed 11 for design review. thanks! :+1:

InfraBot: reminder: create RFC under /rfc/ with rollout checklist and metrics before Wed sync.
